The House Bill 249 By: Representatives Dickey of Committee on Energy, Utilities and Telecommunications offers the 134th, Anderson of the 10th, Huddleston of the 72nd, Drenner of the 85th, and Campbell of the 171st following substitute to HB 249:
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Article 1 of Chapter 3 of Title 46 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to generation and distribution of electricity generally, so as to revise provisions relating … revise provisions relating to the waiver of certain requirements of such agreements; to provide for the certification by the Environmental Protection Division of the Department of Natural Resources that solar power facility agreements meet certain requirements; to provide civil penalties; to provide an exception; to revise and provide for definitions; to provide an effective date; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1. Article 1 of … the property of a landowner pursuant to a solar power facility agreement, the grantee shall obtain from the division a certification that the solar power facility agreement complies with the requirements of this part.
(b) The division shall issue or refuse to issue to a grantee the certification required under subsection (a) of this Code section within ten 30 days of receiving a fully executed solar power facility agreement from the grantee along with any other information that the division may require. If the division determines that such solar power facility agreement does not comply with the requirements of this part, the grantee shall cure such deficiency through a written modification of the solar power facility agreement that is signed by the grantee and the landowner. The division shall, within ten 30 days of receiving such written modification and any other information the division may require, determine if such modification brings the solar power facility agreement in compliance with the requirements of this part and, if so, issue to the grantee the certification required under subsection (a) of this Code section. (c)(1) Any Except as provided in paragraph (3) of this subsection, any grantee that installs or otherwise constructs any solar power facilities on the property of a landowner pursuant to a solar power facility agreement prior to obtaining a certification from the division under subsection (a) of this Code section shall be … the property of the landowner. (2) The civil penalty provided for in paragraph (1) of this subsection shall be recoverable in a civil action brought in any court of competent jurisdiction by the Attorney General, the division, or any district attorney." attorney. (3) If the division fails to issue or refuse to issue to a grantee the certification required under subsection (a) of this Code section within 30 days of receiving from the grantee a fully executed solar power facility agreement or a written modification to a solar power facility agreement as required under subsection (b) of this Code section, then the division shall be deemed to have issued such certification to the grantee and the grantee shall not be subject to the civil penalty provided for in paragraph (1) of this subsection."
SECTION 2. This Act shall become effective upon its approval by the Governor or upon its becoming law without such approval.
SECTION 3. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
